requirement: Count words per file from the command line, printing results to stdout and diagnostics to stderr, returning 0, 1 when any file is missing, or 2 on a usage error, and adding a total line when several files are named.
skeleton: main(argv) defaulting to sys.argv[1:], a usage branch on stderr, a per-file loop catching FileNotFoundError to stderr, aligned counts on stdout and a total when more than one name was given.
caption: A small word-count command line tool tested with pytest's capsys fixture, using sys and pathlib from the standard library. main(argv=None) takes the arguments after the program name, falling back to sys.argv[1:] when argv is None, and returns an exit code instead of calling sys.exit so tests can assert it directly. With no file names it prints a usage line to sys.stderr and returns 2. For each name it reads the file as UTF-8 with Path.read_text; a FileNotFoundError is caught, a message of the form wordcount: NAME: no such file goes to sys.stderr, the status becomes 1 and the loop continues with the next file. Each readable file prints its word count, counted with str.split() so runs of spaces and newlines collapse, right-aligned in six columns followed by the name. When more than one name was given it also prints a total line over the readable files. Results only ever go to stdout and diagnostics only ever go to stderr. The fixture asserts the exact stdout for one file and for two files with a total, that a missing file leaves the other results and total on stdout while its message lands on stderr with exit code 1, that no arguments give exit code 2 with empty stdout and a usage message on stderr, and that sys.argv is read when argv is omitted.

plan.intent: Test a CLI's output streams with capsys
constraints: Word counts go to stdout right-aligned in six columns
Missing files are reported on stderr and set exit code 1 without stopping
No arguments print usage to stderr and return 2
A total line appears only when several files are named
argv defaults to sys.argv without the program name

rationale.teaches: Returning an exit code from main and separating stdout from stderr so capsys.readouterr can assert each stream exactly.
rationale.why: Printing errors to stdout or counting the program name as an argument looks fine in a terminal and only shows up when a test reads the two streams separately.

ops.docstring: A tiny word-count CLI that keeps results and errors on separate streams.

ops.source:
def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Print word counts per file; return 0, 1 if a file is missing, 2 on usage."""
    names = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    if not names:
        print("usage: wordcount FILE...", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    status = 0
    total = 0
    for name in names:
        try:
            text = Path(name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            print(f"wordcount: {name}: no such file", file=sys.stderr)
            status = 1
            continue
        words = len(text.split())
        total += words
        print(f"{words:>6} {name}")
    if len(names) > 1:
        print(f"{total:>6} total")
    return status

candidates.why_wrong: The missing-file message is printed to stdout, mixing diagnostics into the results.
A total line is printed even for a single file argument.
A missing file is reported but the exit code stays 0.
The default keeps the program name in sys.argv and treats it as a file to count.
split on a single space does not collapse newlines or runs of spaces, so counts are wrong.
